raw_response: Banks reported the FDIC special assessment as a notable item that significantly impacted expenses. In late 2023, one bank recorded an approximately $1.7 billion charge related to regional bank failures, while another reported $1.9 billion in non-interest expense for the year including this assessment. In the first half of 2024, a third bank noted $336 million of expense for the FDIC special assessment, which was included in their updated full-year guidance. Banks generally excluded these assessments when calculating "excluding notable items" metrics to show underlying performance trends, such as pre-tax margins and earnings per share.
